learning_outcomes.text: Students have a holistic view of digitalization in the production environment and can distinguish the essential existing technologies. After completing the module, students differentiate between the various technologies of networked production and assign them to possible manufacturing processes. They distinguish between reality and virtuality and explain the benefits of intensive data collection and use against the background of economic efficiency and sustainability.

After completing the module, students delineate necessary data streams within a digitized production and integrate standards regarding data collection and storage. They explain the use of adaptive manufacturing systems with a holistic view of production areas and illustrate the benefits within production-technically defined value chains.

syllabus_topics: Foundations: Value chain, Industrial Revolutions, past and present technology drivers, manufacturing processes in the context of efficiency – ecology – sustainability
Digital Twins: Product/process/resource modeling, communication between reality and virtuality, real-time synchronization, simulation models, virtual commissioning

Networking of Machine Tools: Holistic and adaptive manufacturing systems, integration of autonomous sensor-based systems, information technology in the context of machine tools, machine-machine communication

Technologies in Networked Production: Internet of Things, cyber-physical systems, cloud computing, service-oriented architectures, standardized interfaces and protocols, industrial bus systems, real-time capability
Data Acquisition and Analysis: Data in the context of product – process – resource, operational data acquisition, data storage, analysis and logging functions

Self-control of Manufacturing and Assembly Systems: Coordination of the value chain, use of autonomous machines and robots, adaptive production units, optimizations with regard to raw material efficiency and CO2 footprint
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a portfolio examination consisting of a semester-long written project report (PSC) and a term paper (HA). The total score is 100 points, with a maximum of 50 points achievable for each of the written project report and the term paper. The experimental work is an ungraded assessment and consists of approximately 3 to 5 experimental tasks.
